lesson.title: Detect bias and prevent harmful feedback
lesson.summary: Detect harmful bias and address feedback that reinforces it.

prerequisites.reason: Bias can arise from origins and selection
A representational shortfall can affect groups.

blocks: A **bias feedback loop** occurs when outputs influence inputs for future operation. Northbridge recommends candidates; resulting hires become its next learning records. Prior mistakes may then be reinforced.

Article 10 examines possible biases likely to affect health/safety, harm fundamental rights or cause prohibited discrimination, especially with such feedback. A prediction’s repetition does not independently validate it.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 10(2)(f), (g); Article 15(4), continuing-learning clause

blocks: **Bias mitigation** means appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate the biases identified through that examination. Start by examining collection, labels, representation and operation against the intended purpose.

An equal-looking aggregate statistic is not conclusive evidence that every relevant group or decision context is protected. Do not infer prohibited discrimination from one unexplained difference either; investigate evidence and applicable law.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 10(2)(f), (g); Article 15(4), continuing-learning clause

blocks: For systems continuing to learn after supply, Article 15(4) requires reducing or eliminating as far as possible the risk of biased outputs influencing future inputs, with appropriate mitigation measures.
Illustrative controls include separately reviewing labels or restricting automatic reuse pending validation. Select controls on evidence rather than declaring one method universally mandatory.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 10(2)(f), (g); Article 15(4), continuing-learning clause

blocks: Case: Northbridge retrains from its own accepted recommendations and reports growing agreement with past hires. That agreement can measure a self-reinforcing pattern rather than better recruitment performance.

Document the identified bias, its likely rights or safety consequence, the control and the evidence after correction. Sensitive personal data is not automatically authorised merely because the project concerns fairness.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 10(2)(f), (g); Article 15(4), continuing-learning clause
